title: How useState knows which state is yours

slides.say: Use state gets no name or ID. So how does React know which state to give back?

slides.code:
const [index, setIndex] = useState(0);
const [show, setShow] = useState(false);
slides.say: React does not parse your code. Hooks rely on a stable call order on every render of the same component.
A simplified picture: React holds an array of state pairs per component, and an index set to zero before each render. Each use state call takes the next pair and moves the index.

slides.text: Skip a Hook with an if, and every later Hook gets the wrong slot.
slides.say: That is why order matters. Skip one call, and every Hook after it reads someone else’s slot. The lint plugin catches most of these mistakes.
